question: What was Ibn Turka's confessional position?
proposition: Ibn Turka was a Shiʿi-Sunni (imamophile), preferring unification and synthesis to sectarian polemic; this was normal in his milieu.
reasoning: Timurid confessional ambiguity was endemic (Hodgson, Masad, court examples, Sufi orders' ʿAlid filiation).
Ibn Turka wrote a Sunni-style manāqib work on ʿAlī, kept Companions in his esoteric works, yet rewrote a Sufi verse to praise the Imams and reserved highest praise for ʿAlī.
His millenarian esotericism, in MK's view, makes either-or labels unhelpful.
